name: Green Day
label: Lookout!
lede: Billie Joe Armstrong and Mike Dirnt were fifteen when they started a band in a Rodeo garage. Their first album cost $675 to make, and by 2024 Wikipedia counts roughly 75 million records sold worldwide.

eras.title: A Rodeo garage, a Berkeley warehouse, $4,000 in dole money
eras.text: Billie Joe Armstrong and Mike Dirnt start Sweet Children as fifteen-year-olds. Larry Livermore, who runs Lookout! Records on money saved from unemployment benefits, puts out their first EP, and 924 Gilman Street in Berkeley becomes their home room.

years.h: [[Billie Joe Armstrong|5d06fe54-485a-4a07-b506-5f6f719448cb]] and [[Mike Dirnt|f332a312-e95b-4413-b6cc-1762a5a6a083]] start a band in a Rodeo garage
years.p: They begin as Desecrated Youth with bassist Sean Hughes and drummer Raj Punjabi, rehearsing in Punjabi's garage in Rodeo, California. They're fifteen. The name Sweet Children comes next.

years.h: Rod's Hickory Pit in Vallejo hosts the first show
years.p: Sweet Children play their first live gig at a restaurant and bar in Vallejo.

years.cap: Sweet Children at 924 Gilman Street, Berkeley, November 1988.
years.h: [[John Kiffmeyer|9eb48aba-297f-42f7-b0f9-73ecc0738ae1]] takes the drums and Dirnt picks up the bass
years.p: Kiffmeyer, who goes by Al Sobrante, replaces Punjabi. When Hughes leaves, Dirnt moves from guitar to bass and the trio is set.
years.xp:
Louder reports the band played a mountain cabin party around their third or fourth show in 1988. Armstrong and Dirnt were barely sixteen.

The room that took them in was 924 Gilman Street: an empty West Berkeley warehouse that volunteers talked the city into letting them fix up, run as an all-ages club.

years.big: "Green Day's a stupid name. It doesn't even mean anything."
years.h: Larry Livermore pays for the first Green Day EP with dole money
years.p: [[Larry Livermore|427f8569-3791-4887-976c-242bb49a573f]] on the new name, which the band picked two weeks before 1,000 Hours came out in April 1989. Livermore says it's Bay Area slang for a day spent smoking weed.
years.xp:
Livermore started Lookout! Records with $4,000 saved from his unemployment benefits. 1,000 Hours sold about 1,000 copies in its first year, Louder reports. The label's Operation Ivy EP had sold around 2,500.

Of the teenagers behind the name he said, "When it came to band stuff, they knew what they wanted to do."

eras.title: A new drummer and a record that sells out on day one
eras.text: John Kiffmeyer leaves for college in September 1990. Tré Cool, who already plays in Livermore's band the Lookouts, takes the stool, and Kerplunk follows.

years.h: Two days and $675 make 39/Smooth
years.p: The first Green Day album for Lookout! comes out in April 1990 with Kiffmeyer still on drums. Lookout! reissues it a year later inside a larger collection.
years.xp: The recording took two days. Louder lists the total bill at $675.

years.cap: Green Day at a backyard party.
years.h: Tré Cool, already a Lookout, takes over the drums
years.p: Kiffmeyer leaves for Humboldt State University. [[Tré Cool|0dcee02c-5d2c-4f5c-9d60-d58a4df32d9e]], who plays in Livermore's band [[The Lookouts|700cf581-cc8c-49c1-93e3-489bf1719255]], steps in and doesn't leave.
years.xp:
Livermore gave Cool his first drum lesson at twelve, Louder says, and a week later the kid was in the Lookouts. His first Green Day show was in November 1990.

Kiffmeyer had left in September to go to college.

years.h: The early EPs collect on 1,039/Smoothed Out Slappy Hours
years.p: Lookout! bundles 39/Smooth with the Slappy and Sweet Children EPs. For most listeners, it's how they first meet the early band.

years.cap: Green Day with Tré Cool at a backyard show in Downey, California.
years.h: Kerplunk sells 10,000 copies the day it comes out
years.p: Cut at Art of Ears in San Francisco for about $2,000, it's the first Green Day album with Cool on drums. Louder says 50,000 copies were out by the end of 1992.
years.xp:
The sessions ran in May and September 1991. It came out in the UK on December 17 and in the US on January 17, 1992. Livermore defended the December date to doubting distributors: "Punks don't follow the record industry calendar."

He had also commissioned cover art of a girl obsessed with Green Day who murders her parents. Wikipedia says some retailers refused to stock it.

eras.title: Reprise, Dookie, and a mud fight
eras.text: Green Day sign to Reprise and get barred from Gilman Street. A year later Dookie has three #1s on Modern Rock Tracks, and Woodstock '94 ends in mud and a security guard's fist.

years.cap: Green Day at 924 Gilman Street, Berkeley.
years.h: Signing with Reprise gets Green Day barred from Gilman
years.p: They play a last show at 924 Gilman Street under a fake name. The all-ages club, strictly against major labels, won't have them back.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the last Gilman show to September 3, 1993, under the name Blair Hess. Louder places a fake-name show at Christmas 1993 and calls the room about half full, with nearly everyone knowing each other.

years.h: Dookie goes in three weeks and ships 20 million in the US
years.p: "Longview", "Basket Case" and "When I Come Around" all reach #1 on Modern Rock Tracks. Dookie wins the 1995 Grammy for Best Alternative Album.
years.xp: When it passed 500,000 copies, Reprise took out a full-page Billboard ad that read "Dookie Is Gold." Louder says the record kept going from there.

years.h: Woodstock '94 turns into a mud fight, and Dirnt loses teeth
years.p: The band starts the fight with the crowd. A security guard mistakes Dirnt for a stage invader and punches out some of his teeth, Wikipedia says.
years.xp: The set was released on vinyl for Record Store Day 2019 as Woodstock 1994.

years.h: Boston's Hatch Shell show ends in a riot
years.p: Green Day get through a shortened seven-song set at Hatch Memorial Shell. Wikipedia counts about 100 injured and 45 arrested.

eras.title: After the hit, darker and stranger
eras.text: Insomniac answers Dookie with an angrier record. Nimrod adds an acoustic ballad. Armstrong's label Adeline Records releases a masked band's album that Green Day won't confirm is theirs for ten years.

years.h: Insomniac answers the hit with a darker record
years.p: Out October 10, 1995, it goes double platinum, which Wikipedia describes as a much darker response to sudden fame.

years.h: Nimrod puts an acoustic ballad on a punk record
years.p: "Good Riddance (Time of Your Life)" wins the MTV Video Music Award for Best Alternative Video. The album also touches surf, ska and folk.

years.h: A free San Francisco City Hall show backs evicted artists
years.p: In November Green Day play for free to protest artist evictions. Warning goes gold, the first Green Day album since Dookie not to reach triple platinum.

years.h: Green Day, in masks, as The Network
years.p: Money Money 2020 comes out on Armstrong's Adeline Records from a band using costumes and aliases. Green Day don't confirm it's them until 2013.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the album's release as September 2003 and notes the band's identity stayed unconfirmed for a decade.

eras.title: Stolen tapes, a rock opera, a Broadway stage
eras.text: The master tapes for the finished album Cigarettes and Valentines are stolen, so Green Day write American Idiot instead. It debuts at #1, wins a Grammy and ends up on Broadway.

years.h: After the stolen tapes, American Idiot hits #1
years.p: The rock opera debuts at the top of the Billboard 200 and sells six million US copies, Green Day's first #1 album.
years.xp:
In 2002 the master tapes of the finished album Cigarettes and Valentines were stolen from the studio. The band scrapped it and started over, and American Idiot was the result.

It won the 2005 Grammy for Best Rock Album. "Boulevard of Broken Dreams" took Record of the Year the following year.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lookout! Records · Wikipedia: Green Day
years.h: Green Day take back their Lookout! masters
years.p: On August 1 they cite a continuing breach of contract over unpaid royalties. Six of Lookout!'s nine staff are laid off.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Green Day's early releases had brought the label $10 million in 1995 alone. Lookout! entered financial reconstruction in December 2009 and closed in January 2012.

years.h: Foxboro Hot Tubs play small Bay Area rooms
years.p: As the garage-rock alter egos, Armstrong, Dirnt and Cool release Stop Drop and Roll!!! on May 20, 2008.

years.cap: Green Day live in Camden, New Jersey, August 3, 2010.
years.h: American Idiot opens on Broadway
years.p: After a run at Berkeley Repertory Theatre in September 2009, the musical opens April 20, 2010. It earns three Tony nominations and wins two, for lighting and scenic design.

eras.title: Three albums in three months, then the Hall
eras.text: ¡Uno!, ¡Dos! and ¡Tré! come out in one fall. Three years later Fall Out Boy induct the band into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, and Revolution Radio ends the Reprise deal.

years.h: ¡Uno!, ¡Dos! and ¡Tré! land within three months
years.p: September 21, November 9 and December 7, 2012, the first Green Day studio records to feature Jason White.

years.cap: Tré Cool at Rock im Park, Germany.
years.h: Fall Out Boy induct Green Day into the Rock Hall
years.p: It's the band's first year of eligibility. Two days earlier, on April 16, they played a show as Sweet Children with Kiffmeyer on drums.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the April 16 gig as their first concert in a year: a Sweet Children set with Kiffmeyer, then a Green Day set.

years.h: Revolution Radio debuts at #1, then Reprise lets go
years.p: Wikipedia counts it as the band's third #1 album. After this record they part ways with Reprise Records.

eras.title: Fourteen albums, one Super Bowl
eras.text: Saviors arrives in January 2024 with a tour alongside the Smashing Pumpkins, Rancid and the Linda Lindas. Two years later, Green Day open Super Bowl LX.

years.h: Saviors arrives with the Pumpkins and Rancid on the bill
years.p: Their fourteenth studio album comes out January 19, 2024, with "One Eyed Bastard" as its fourth single. The Saviors Tour has the Smashing Pumpkins, Rancid and the Linda Lindas.
play: The American Dream Is Killing Me

years.h: Green Day open Super Bowl LX
years.p: On February 8 they open with an instrumental "Good Riddance", then play "Holiday", "Boulevard of Broken Dreams" and "American Idiot".
years.xp: Wikipedia says the performance left out political references and got mixed reactions from fans.
